calibration.rule: weight = base ^ (1/T), T = TVI / tviDivisor. base = 1/seed (A/B/C), tier table value (D), 1 (E).

cs2.note: Approved TVI; weights final. Do not recalibrate.

ccRules.bestResultOnly: An organisation receives only the highest points obtained by one of its participants in a competition; lower results are not redistributed.
ccRules.tieRule: Rank by points. On equal points, eligible clubs (2+ scoring top-8 finishes) rank above ineligible ones. A tie for 1st among clubs eligible to win (eligible + at least one title win) is broken by better single results (Olympic medal logic); any remaining tie shares the rank. A club without a title win cannot be ranked 1st.

seedMethodology.intro: Every method resolves to the same two fields the simulator consumes: a STRENGTH RANK within the field, and a CONFIDENCE grade. Confidence is separate from title volatility and does a different job — volatility says how much the title scrambles outcomes, confidence says how much we trust the seed. A weak seed widens the simulated spread even in a low-volatility title. Record also the snapshot date and whether the roster changed after it: a rating attaches to five players, not a logo.

A.label: A · Actual seed / world rank
A.what: Published numeric ranking the ecosystem itself uses to invite or seed.
A.whenToUse: First choice wherever it exists — gives ratings as well as ranks, so gaps are measurable.
A.example: CS2 — Valve Regional Standings. Chess — FIDE / Chess.com rapid.
A.watchOutFor: Snapshot must predate the event; ratings attach to a roster.

B.label: B · Most recent event / league form
B.what: Finishing order from a recent competition the same teams contested.
B.whenToUse: Franchised or closed circuits where the field has just played each other.
B.watchOutFor: One event is a small sample; prefer a season table.

C.label: C · Power ranking
C.whenToUse: Cross-region titles with no official ladder.
C.watchOutFor: Poor update cadence, opaque method. Record source and date.

D.label: D · Cohort seeding (High/Med/Low)
D.what: Banded strength by region and international pedigree.
D.whenToUse: Titles where regions rarely meet and ordinals would be false precision.
D.example: LoL — LCK/LPL High; top LEC/AMER/PAC Med; rest Low.
D.watchOutFor: Sample WITHIN the band each run — never collapse a band to one rank.

E.label: E · No credible seed
E.whenToUse: Declare it rather than forcing a proxy; simulator treats the field as flat.
E.watchOutFor: Being explicit beats a fabricated seed that looks authoritative.

titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT MODEL — how a band becomes a number the simulator can use
seedRationale: A cohort is not a seed, it is a RANGE. The simulator never collapses a band to a single rank — that would create artificial ties and understate variance. Instead each cohort maps to a latent strength distribution: a mean position (the midpoint of its band) and a spread (how uncertain we are within the band). On every run each team draws a strength value from its own distribution, the field is re-ranked by those draws, and the resulting order becomes that run's finishing order. Two independent noise sources are combined: SEED UNCERTAINTY (we do not know the order inside a cohort) and TITLE VOLATILITY (the title scrambles outcomes regardless of seed). They add in quadrature — sigma_total = SQRT(sigma_within^2 + sigma_title^2) — because they are independent. This is why the same machinery serves every seed method: a VRS rating gives a precise mean and a small sigma_within; a cohort gives a coarse mean and a large one. Change a team's cohort and its mean moves; change the TVI and every team's spread moves together.
Bands derive automatically from the cohort dropdowns above — reassign a team and every band, mu and sigma updates. Only the two blue cells below are inputs.
Simulator draw, per run and per team:  strength = mu + NORM.INV(RAND(), 0, total sigma)  →  rank the 16 draws ascending  →  that run's finishing order  →  points from block 2.

Sanity check from EWC26: all 7 High-cohort teams finished top 8. The single miss was Karmine Corp (Medium) at 2nd — so a Medium team reaching a final is roughly the tail event this model should produce occasionally, not never.

titles.name: PUBG Mobile
titles.description: Battle royale. Listed on Liquipedia as 'PUBG Mobile World Cup 2026'. Every placement 1-8 pays a DIFFERENT club-point value — no shared bands, unlike the playoff titles.
titles.fieldNote: All 32 teams with exact placements and prize money from the Liquipedia prize table. Seed column is deliberately empty — see the seed note in block 3. Qualification route and region are recorded as data, not used as a seed.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED — METHOD E, DELIBERATELY NONE
seedRationale: Why no seed. Every team qualified by winning or placing in its own regional points race, so the only ranking that exists is WITHIN a region — there is no cross-region ladder that would let us say a 3rd-placed Türkiye team is stronger or weaker than a 2nd-placed SEA team. Manufacturing one would be a guess dressed as data. The 2026 result supports leaving it out: the top eight came from six different regions, and the champion, S2G Esports, qualified 3rd of four from Türkiye. What method E means in the model: every team shares the same mean strength, so outcomes are driven entirely by the title sigma. Expected club points are identical for all 32 teams at 3,050 / 32 = 95.3 per team. That is the correct representation of a title we cannot forecast. Region and qualification route are recorded above as data so that, once several editions exist, we can TEST whether region predicts placement — and upgrade this title to method D (cohort) only if the evidence supports it.
This block is the evidence base for revisiting method E later. If one region were to dominate the top 8 across several editions, cohort seeding would become justified.

titles.name: Fortnite Reload
titles.description: Duos battle royale. Listed on Liquipedia as 'Reload Elite Series 2026 - Championship'. Same BR point curve as PUBG Mobile: every placement 1-8 pays a different value.
titles.fieldNote: All 40 duos with exact placements and prize money. Tier column is the hybrid seed input — default is Field for everyone, which behaves exactly as method E until you promote a duo to Elite.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · HYBRID SEED — WHY, AND THE TRAP TO AVOID
seedRationale: The hybrid. Default is method E: every duo shares one mean strength, so the title sigma alone drives outcomes. Promoting a duo to Elite in the Tier column gives it a stronger mean while the rest of the field stays undifferentiated — mechanically this is a two-cohort version of method D, with a small top band and one large flat band. It is the right shape when a handful of entrants are genuinely stronger but the remaining field cannot be ordered. THE TRAP: seed on RELOAD form, not Fortnite reputation. EWC26 is the evidence. Peterbot, widely rated the best Fortnite player in the world, finished 12th. Bugha, the 2019 World Cup champion, finished 22nd. EpikWhale finished 37th-38th. Meanwhile the winners, vic0 and Malibuca, arrived on the back of consecutive Reload LAN wins. Reload is a distinct mode with its own skillset, and general Fortnite pedigree predicted almost nothing here. If the Elite tier is populated from name recognition it will make the model worse than method E, not better. Populate it only from recent Reload-format results, and keep it small - two to four duos.
With every duo set to Field the Elite band is empty and the model is pure method E — expected points identical for all 40 duos at 3,050 / 40 = 76.3.

OPEN QUESTION — mixed-club duos. Ten of the 40 duos pair players from different clubs (marked 'Mixed'). It is not established how the Club Championship allocates points for those, and no mixed duo finished top 8 except 2nd place (Momsy of Lyost with SkyJump of Ravens), neither of whom is a CC top-24 club, so it cannot be verified from the data we hold. Resolve before simulating this title.

ANOMALY — HavoK by Vitality finished 4th, worth 300 points, but Team Vitality scored 0 in Fortnite. Either HavoK counts as a separate club, or the entry was ineligible for club points (the Clubs page marks some entries as not eligible due to joint ventures or late signings). Worth confirming, as it affects how partner-brand entries are modelled. RESOLVED: with all 25 titles built, crediting the 300 to Team Vitality puts them 300 above their official 3,300, and removing it reconciles them exactly. The entry is therefore joined as its own club, HavoK by Vitality, not as a Vitality entry.

titles.description: 1v1 racing. Seeds from the Elite Cup 2026 final standings — Ubisoft Nadeo's official Road-to-EWC ladder, method A.
titles.fieldNote: All 32 players. Seed is the field ranked 1-32 by Elite Cup finishing position; the raw Elite Cup rank is kept alongside so the gap between ladder form and event result stays visible.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED SOURCE — Elite Cup 2026
seedRationale: The Elite Cup is Ubisoft Nadeo's official Road-to-EWC ladder, run online from February to May 2026 across ten map-nations, with 126 ranked participants. It is the only published pre-event ranking for Trackmania, it is the mechanism that actually awarded EWC slots, and it is ordinal rather than a rating — so seeds carry rank but no strength gaps. WHAT 2026 SHOWED: the ladder did not transfer cleanly to the LAN. Elite Cup winner Binkss finished 9th-12th; 2nd-placed GranaDy took 5th-6th; 3rd-placed Massa 9th-12th; 4th-placed Mudda 17th-20th. The EWC champion Gwen came from 9th on the ladder and the runner-up Epos from 18th. That is a weaker seed-to-outcome relationship than the TVI of 22 implies, and worth watching: Trackmania is scored as a low-volatility title on the strength of an elite that converts, but the ladder rank itself proved a poor predictor of finishing position at this event.

seedRationale: The EPT leaderboard is the season-long ESL circuit ranking and the best seed source we have for Dota: it carries numeric points, so strength gaps are measurable rather than ordinal — Tundra on 16,710 versus Execration on 48 is a real distance, not just 24 places. First, five EWC entrants (Rune Eaters, LGD Gaming, Level UP, L1 TEAM, IC x Insanity) do not appear on the leaderboard at all; they are seeded last here, but that is an assumption, not a measurement — and Rune Eaters promptly finished 5th-8th, so the assumption was wrong for them. Second, the leaderboard is not an EWC qualification ladder: EPT #1 Tundra Esports did not attend at all. WHAT 2026 SHOWED: mixed. The champion PVISION came from EPT #2, and Spirit and Falcons converted top-seven seeds into top-eight finishes. But Aurora at EPT #3 went out in 9th-12th, Xtreme Gaming at #4 in 13th-16th, and Vici Gaming reached 4th from #16. That spread is consistent with a TVI of 55 — favourites go deep more often than not, but conversion is unreliable.

titles.name: Tekken 8
titles.description: 1v1 fighting game. Seeds from the Tekken World Tour 2026 Global Points Standings — method A, 250 ranked players with numeric points.
titles.fieldNote: All 32 players. Seed ranks the field by TWT global points; the raw TWT rank sits alongside so the gap between circuit form and event result stays visible.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED SOURCE — TWT 2026 Global Points, and a serious warning
seedRationale: The Tekken World Tour Global Points Standings rank 250 players with numeric season points, and EWC 2026 sits on the TWT circuit, so on paper this is a strong method A source — comparable in quality to VRS or the EPT leaderboard. IN PRACTICE IT PREDICTED ALMOST NOTHING AT THIS EVENT. Champion M. Zubair entered as TWT #52, seeded 27th of 32. The top of the circuit collapsed: TWT #1 ATIF finished 17th-24th, #3 Rangchu 17th-24th, #6 Mulgold 17th-24th, #7 Knee 25th-32nd, #10 Meo-IL 25th-32nd. Meanwhile Raef at TWT #81 reached 5th-8th and Numan Ch at #61 did the same. TWO READINGS, and the data cannot yet separate them. Either Tekken's TVI of 36 is far too low and this is a genuinely high-variance title, or TWT points measure something different from single-event LAN strength — they accumulate across a season of open tournaments, so they reward attendance volume as much as peak quality. The second reading is supported by the fact that the 2025 EWC champion Ulsan, who is a proven LAN performer, entered at TWT #9 and finished 5th-8th. DO NOT recalibrate the TVI from this single event — but flag Tekken as the title where seed quality most needs a second edition of evidence.

NOTE on unmatched clubs: Yagami (3rd) and AK (25th-32nd) carry no club tag on Liquipedia. Weibo Gaming shows 0 points in Tekken on the CC standings, which is consistent with AK being their entry, but this is inference — verify before relying on it.

titles.name: Street Fighter 6
titles.description: HYBRID SEED. CPT 2026 points where they exist (13 of 32); a manually assigned Tier for the other 19. Both resolve to a mean and a sigma, so the engine treats them identically.
titles.fieldNote: All 32 players. CPT-ranked players carry a numeric seed. For the 19 unranked, set Tier in the dropdown — base it on RECENT form (last 12-18 months), not career honours; see block 3 for why. Tier is greyed out for CPT-ranked players, whose seed comes from points.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · WHY HYBRID — CPT POINTS PLUS A MANUAL TIER
seedRationale: The Capcom Pro Tour 2026 Global Leaderboard covers only 13 of the 32 entrants — the rest arrived via auto-qualification, the Last Chance Qualifier, or regional routes that do not feed the global table. Leaving all 19 as one flat bucket is demonstrably wrong: FOUR of the eight top-eight finishers were unranked (Hibiki 2nd, Yamaguchi 4th, MenaRD 5th-8th, Leshar 5th-8th). Hence the Tier column. BASE THE TIER ON RECENT FORM, NOT CAREER HONOURS. This is the important instruction, and 2026 is the evidence. A pedigree-based tier would have promoted the decorated veterans - and every one of them collapsed: Xiaohai 25th-32nd, Itabashi Zangief 25th-32nd, Daigo 17th-24th, Xian 17th-24th, Phenom 17th-24th. Meanwhile the two unranked players who reached the podium places, Hibiki and Yamaguchi, are recent-era competitors rather than crossover legends. MenaRD is the one big name who delivered. Use Capcom Cup 11/12 finishes, EWC 2025 SF6 and Evo 2025/26 as the basis; a name that has not placed deep in the last 12-18 months belongs in Medium or Low regardless of its trophy cabinet. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: the Capcom Cup auto-qualified list looks predictive (five of seven made top 8) but is CONTAMINATED — winning EWC itself grants a Capcom Cup slot, so it is partly an output of this event. Using it would leak the result into the seed. ALSO NOTE: CPT was weak even where it had coverage — #1 Micky finished 9th-12th, #3 Punk 25th-32nd, #4 Kilzyou 17th-24th, and champion Craime entered at #9. Across Tekken, SF6, Fatal Fury and Fortnite Reload the same pattern holds: season-long circuit points and career reputation both underperform, while recent format-specific form does not.
Tier bands start at position 14 because the 13 CPT-ranked players occupy seeds 1-13. Bands re-tile automatically as you reassign tiers. Defaults are all Medium — change them before simulating.

titles.name: Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves
titles.description: Seed method E — no credible pre-event ranking exists. The reasoning is in block 3; this is a deliberate choice, not a gap in the research.
titles.fieldNote: All 32 players. Seed column intentionally empty — every player shares the same mean strength under method E.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · WHY METHOD E
seedRationale: Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves launched in 2025 and EWC 2026 is only its second appearance. There is no season-long ranking equivalent to the Tekken World Tour or Capcom Pro Tour tables: the SNK World Championship Finals is where this event QUALIFIES PLAYERS TO, not a ladder they arrive with. Liquipedia carries no global points standing for the title. So there is genuinely nothing to seed from — declaring that is more useful than constructing a proxy from reputation. The temptation would be to seed on FGC pedigree, since several entrants are decorated in other games — Xiaohai, GO1, Nemo, Poongko all have major titles elsewhere. The 2026 result argues against exactly that: GO1 finished 13th-16th, Xiaohai 17th-24th, Poongko 13th-16th, while the winner DarkAngel and runner-up mi2ha4 are CotW specialists rather than crossover names. This mirrors the Fortnite Reload lesson — in a young title, general reputation is a poor guide, and format-specific form is what matters. WHEN TO REVISIT: once SNK publishes a season-long points table, or after a second or third edition provides seed-versus-outcome data of its own, this should be upgraded to method C or D. Until then every player shares one mean and outcomes come entirely from the title sigma.

titles.name: Teamfight Tactics
titles.seedSource: Rule: CN + KR = High, else Medium
titles.description: Squads format, 4 players per club. Method D applied: cohorts are assigned by rule — High for Chinese and South Korean clubs, Medium for all others. The rule and its evidence are in block 3.
titles.fieldNote: All 16 teams. Cohort is applied automatically from Region by the rule above — change a Region and set the Cohort to match, or override the Cohort directly. Region is inferred from club origin; the event page does not record which qualifier each club entered through.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED — METHOD E TODAY, WITH A REGIONAL CASE FOR UPGRADING
seedRationale: THE RULE: High cohort = clubs from China or South Korea. Medium = everyone else. Applied programmatically from the Region column, so it is reproducible rather than hand-picked club by club. WHY: there is no pre-event ranking for TFT — teams arrive through separate regional qualifiers that produce no cross-region ordering — but region itself carried a clear signal in 2026. The CN/KR cohort converted five of seven entries into top-eight finishes (71%); everyone else converted three of nine (33%), against a 50% baseline. The top three were all Chinese: Team Vision, Aurora Gaming and AG.AL International. TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS WORTH KNOWING. Flash Wolves (Taiwan) sits in Medium because the rule is CN and KR specifically, yet they finished 4th — the single biggest cost of drawing the line that way. Including Taiwan would raise the High cohort to 75% conversion, but that would be fitting the rule to one result rather than to a stated principle. ZETA DIVISION (Japan) likewise stays Medium and finished 9th-12th, which supports the exclusion. STILL ONE EDITION OF EVIDENCE. TFT carries a high TVI of 65, so the cohort structure and the volatility term are pulling against each other by design: even High-cohort clubs will scatter widely in simulation. Recompute the regional block below after each new edition — a second consistent year would make this rule solid rather than provisional.
Random baseline for top-8 rate is 50% (8 of 16 teams). Recompute after each edition to test whether the CN/KR rule holds.

titles.name: Rainbow Six Siege
titles.description: Seed method A — Six Invitational 2027 Global Points Standings. EWC awards no SI points and the later season events were unplayed, so that table is a clean pre-event snapshot.
titles.fieldNote: All 22 teams, ranked by SI points. Two teams (Al-Ula Club, MIBR.LOS) do not appear on the standings and are seeded last — an assumption, flagged in Notes.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED SOURCE — SI 2027 Global Standings
seedRationale: Why this source is clean. Ubisoft's Six Invitational points are the ecosystem's own ranking and they decide SI qualification, so teams take them seriously. Critically, EWC itself awards NO SI points, and the two later season events on the table (Regional Leagues 2, November Major) were unplayed at the time of writing — so the standings are a genuine pre-event snapshot built from the Regional Kickoff, the May Major and Regional Leagues 1. No result leakage. ONE DISCREPANCY WORTH KNOWING: Liquipedia's own rank column does not order strictly by points — FaZe are listed 1st on 1,610 while DarkZero sit 2nd on 1,890. The seeds here are built from POINTS descending, since points are the measurable quantity; the published rank is kept alongside so the difference is visible. WHAT 2026 SHOWED: middling. Champion FaZe entered as the 2nd-highest-pointed team and DarkZero, top on points, took 3rd — the very top converted well. Below that it fell apart: ENTERPRISE (seed 3) finished 13th-16th, Shopify Rebellion (seed 4) 17th-18th, and Falcons (seed 6) 9th-12th, while runner-up FURIA came from seed 12, Geekay reached 4th from seed 18, and Team Secret made the top eight from seed 20 on just 80 points. This is now a recurring shape across titles: the elite converts, the middle of the seed list predicts very little. Worth holding in mind when the TVI is eventually recalibrated — R6 carries a low 30, which fits the top of the field but not the rest of it.

titles.name: Warzone
titles.description: Trios battle royale, listed on Liquipedia as 'Warzone Resurgence Series 2026 Championship'. Seed method B — qualification route and timing, not a ranking.
titles.fieldNote: All 32 trios, ordered by the qualification-route seed. Six seeds are marked INFERRED — the qualifier result and the EWC field disagree on the org name, so the slot is matched by field position rather than a verified link.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED — QUALIFICATION ROUTE AND TIMING (METHOD B)
seedRationale: There is no Warzone ranking to seed from, but qualification timing carries information: the strongest rosters tend to qualify first, at the two LAN events, while later online opens fill the remaining slots. The seed order is therefore: invited champion, then DH Birmingham, then DH Atlanta, then the regional online opens in the priority order supplied — North America, LATAM North, LATAM South, Europe, APAC, MENA. Within each route, teams are ordered by their finishing position in that qualifier. SIX SEEDS ARE INFERRED, marked amber. In those cases the qualifier winner and the EWC entrant carry different org names — Birmingham's 3rd place was Los Corillos while Leviatán occupies that slot in the field, the NA 6th qualifier carried no org tag at all, and so on. The slot is matched by position in the field rather than a verified link, so treat those six as assumptions. NOTE ON RAVENS ESPORTS: they qualified twice, winning the MENA online open and placing 4th at Birmingham. The earlier LAN route is used, which is the whole logic of this method. WHAT 2026 SHOWED: the route seed was weak, as a TVI of 75 would predict. Champion G2 came from Atlanta 5th (seed 7) and runner-up T1 from Atlanta 8th (seed 10), so the Atlanta cohort did convert — but Birmingham winners Team Falcons finished 16th, and the invited defending champions Twisted Minds took 4th. Meanwhile Gentle Mates and Ekletyc reached 5th and 6th from the European online open, seeds 22 and 23. For a high-volatility battle royale this is roughly what the model should expect: a real but weak signal, better than method E and far short of a ranking.
Use this block to test whether route order predicts anything across future editions — if the LAN routes keep outperforming the late online opens, method B is justified for this title.

titles.name: VALORANT
titles.seedSource: Riot GPR, End of Masters London (21 Jun 26)
titles.description: Seeded from Riot's own VALORANT Global Power Rankings — the 'End of Masters London' snapshot, dated 21 June 2026, eleven days before this event. A clean pre-event ranking with numeric power scores.
titles.fieldNote: All 16 teams, seeded by GPR power score. The score is kept alongside the rank because it is a genuine strength measure — the gap from NRG on 1,472 to AG.AL on 1,181 is information a bare ranking would lose.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED SOURCE — RIOT GPR, AND ITS TIMING PROBLEM
seedRationale: This is the cleanest seed source in the workbook. Riot maintains the GPR themselves: a model with numeric power scores covering 48 teams across all four VCT leagues, so cross-region comparison is built into the number rather than assumed. That is exactly what the Rainbow Six and Dota sources lack. AND THE TIMING IS RIGHT. Riot publishes event-pinned snapshots, so the 'End of Masters London' table dated 21 June 2026 sits eleven days before this event began on 2 July. No result leakage, no stale season. Method A, not a proxy. WHAT 2026 SHOWED: the seed underperformed, and unusually it failed at the TOP rather than the middle. GPR #1 Paper Rex, on 1,605 points and 200 clear of second, finished 13th-16th — the largest single miss in the workbook. Global Esports (seed 8) also went out in 13th-16th. Meanwhile champion 100 Thieves came from seed 7, BBL Esports reached 4th from seed 13, Gentle Mates made the top eight from seed 14, and Karmine Corp entered last on 1,126 points and still finished 9th-12th. That inverts the pattern seen in chess, Trackmania, Tekken and R6, where the elite converted and the middle scattered. Here the elite was the problem. Two readings, unresolvable from one event: either Valorant genuinely punishes favourites more than the TVI of 50 allows, or a strong GPR score built on VCT league form does not transfer to a short offline bracket. WORTH NOTING: GPR #2 Leviatán, #4 T1, #6 Kiwoom DRX and #9 Fnatic did not attend. This was not the world's strongest sixteen, which caps how much any seed could have explained.

titles.name: MLBB Mid Season Cup
titles.description: The men's MLBB event at EWC. Cohort seeding applied by rule from the qualifying league: MPL Indonesia and MPL Philippines = High, other SEA leagues = Medium, everything else = Low.
titles.fieldNote: All 25 teams. League of origin comes from the official qualification table. Where a club fields two teams, the canonical column maps the entry to the parent club — only the better finisher earns club points, so reconciliation takes a MAX over the canonical name.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT RULE AND HOW IT PERFORMED
seedRationale: THE RULE: High = MPL Indonesia and MPL Philippines. Medium = the other Southeast Asian leagues (Malaysia, Singapore, Cambodia, Myanmar, Thailand). Low = everything else — EECA, Turkey, MENA, Americas, East Asia, India. Applied from the qualifying league recorded on the official qualification table, so it derives from sourced data rather than inference about club origin. IT SEPARATED WELL. High converted three of four entries into top-eight finishes (75%), Medium three of six (50%), Low two of fifteen (13%), against a baseline of 32%. That is the cleanest cohort separation in the workbook and supports treating MPL ID and PH as the strongest leagues. BUT THE WINNER CAME FROM LOW. Team Spirit qualified through MCC, the EECA circuit, and won the whole thing — the first EECA club to take an MLBB major. Yangon Galacticos took second from Myanmar, a Medium league. So the rule ranked the FIELD well while missing the PODIUM entirely: neither finalist came from a High cohort league, and the best High finish was ONIC in 3rd. This is the same tension seen elsewhere — a seed that predicts who makes the top eight is not automatically a seed that predicts who wins. With a TVI of 60 the model should already expect upsets of this size; worth rechecking after the next edition rather than adjusting either input now.

entries.notes: first EECA club to win an MLBB major
second Team Falcons entry — only the better finisher scores
second Team Liquid entry — only the better finisher scores

titles.name: Apex Legends
titles.description: Run as the ALGS 2026 Split 1 Playoffs. Cohorts applied by rule from Split 1 Pro League regional finishing position.
titles.fieldNote: All 40 trios. Region and Pro League placement come from the four Split 1 regional standings pages, so the cohort derives from sourced data. ZEDI ESPORTS' 300 points are voided — squad signed past the Team Deadline.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT RULE AND HOW IT PERFORMED
seedRationale: THE RULE, as specified: High = the top 4 qualifiers from APAC North, top 5 from EMEA, top 3 from APAC South and top 5 from Americas, by Split 1 Pro League finishing position. Low = the bottom 2 qualifiers from each region. Medium = everyone else, plus the invited team. Applied programmatically from the four regional standings pages, so it is reproducible rather than hand-assigned. IT SEPARATED WEAKLY. High converted five of seventeen entries into top-eight finishes (29%), Medium three of fifteen (20%), Low none of eight (0%), against a 20% baseline. The Low cohort behaved exactly as intended — no bottom-2 regional qualifier reached the top eight. But High barely beat chance, and Medium sat exactly on it. THE TOP OF THE PRO LEAGUE DID NOT TRANSFER AT ALL. Regional winners finished: Ninjas in Pyjamas (Americas 1st) 15th, Aurora Gaming (EMEA 1st) 28th, ZETA DIVISION (APAC-N 1st) 5th, Wolves Esports (APAC-S 1st) 7th. Champions UNLIMIT came from APAC North 3rd, runner-up Team Vision from Americas 3rd, and third-placed Sentinels from Americas 7th — a Medium seed. Of the 40-team field, only two of the eight regional top-two finishers made the EWC top eight. Pro League form predicts who is bad here far better than it predicts who is good. TWO INFERRED MAPPINGS, flagged amber in the rows: ZEDI ESPORTS is matched to the HUSS slot (Americas 11th) — consistent with their points being voided for signing a squad past the deadline — and TLN Pirates to the Make Europe Great Again slot (EMEA 7th). Neither link is stated on Liquipedia.
Baseline top-8 rate is 8/40 = 20%. Note top-8 counts use earned points, so ZEDI's voided 4th still counts as a top-8 finish here — the void affects club points, not sporting placement.

entries.notes: VOIDED — squad signed past the Team Deadline
INVITED as defending champion, not via the Pro League qualification slots
listed as HAVOC in the Pro League standings
INFERRED: occupies the Make Europe Great Again slot (EMEA 7th)

titles.name: Honor of Kings
titles.description: Run as the Honor of Kings World Cup 2026. Cohorts assigned by rule from the qualifying league: Chinese teams and the top 2 from Malaysia = High, rest of SEA = Medium, everyone else = Low.
titles.fieldNote: All 20 teams. Qualifying event and region come from the official qualification table, so the cohort derives from sourced data. Several clubs compete under partner-brand names; the canonical column resolves them.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT RULE AND HOW IT PERFORMED
seedRationale: THE RULE: High = Chinese teams (the KPL Spring qualifier plus the invited defending champion) and the top two from MKL Spring, Malaysia. Medium = the rest of Southeast Asia — MKL 3rd, all three IKL Indonesia qualifiers, plus the Philippines, Thailand, Taiwan and Vietnam slots. Low = everyone else: Korea, Brazil and India. Applied from the qualifying event recorded on the official qualification table. IT SEPARATED SHARPLY AT THE TOP. All four High teams made the top eight — a 100% conversion rate — and they took first, second, third and a 5th-8th. Medium converted three of ten (30%) and Low one of six (17%), against a 40% baseline. This is the cleanest High-cohort result anywhere in the workbook: the two Chinese entries finished 1st and 2nd, and the two Malaysian top-two seeds took 3rd and a 5th-8th. MEDIUM AND LOW ARE THE WEAK PART. Both landed below the 40% baseline, so the rule is really binary — China plus the Malaysian elite versus everyone else — rather than three genuinely ordered tiers. If a future edition repeats this, collapsing Medium and Low into one band would lose almost nothing. ONE JUDGEMENT CALL: Deep Cross Gaming qualified through GCS, the Taiwanese league, which is not strictly Southeast Asia. Placed in Medium as Garena groups it with the SEA structure; flagged in the row. They finished 13th-16th, so the choice did not affect the outcome.

entries.notes: Taiwan grouped with SEA — judgement call

titles.name: CrossFire
titles.description: Cohorts assigned by rule from the qualifying route: invited plus all Chinese CFPL qualifiers plus the SEA Masters and CFBL winners = High; other SEA Masters/CFBL qualifiers = Medium; the West and MENA routes = Low.
titles.fieldNote: All 16 teams. Qualifying route traced through the four CrossFire Stars points tables (CFPL China, CFBL Brazil, CFWL West, SEA Masters), so the cohort derives from sourced data.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT RULE AND HOW IT PERFORMED
seedRationale: THE RULE: High = the invited team, all five Chinese CFPL qualifiers, and the winners of SEA Masters Summer (Team Stallions) and CFBL Points (ROC Esports). Medium = the other qualifiers from those two events — Team Liquid and Natus Vincere from CFBL, Execration from SEA Masters. Low = everyone else, which here means the three CFWL West qualifiers and the three MENA teams through the EUMENA Regional Finals. THE LOW CALL WAS THE STRONG ONE. Low converted one of six into the top eight (17%) against a 50% baseline, and five of the six finished 9th or worse. High converted five of seven (71%) and took first, third and fourth. HIGH AND MEDIUM DID NOT SEPARATE. Medium converted two of three (67%), effectively the same rate as High — but on only three teams, so the comparison is thin. Team Liquid, a Medium seed from CFBL 2nd, reached the final and out-placed every Chinese team except BaiSha. THE CHINESE BLOCK SPLIT. CFPL 1st and 2nd finished 1st and 3rd, but CFPL 4th and 5th (Evolution Power, Qing Jiu Club) finished 9th-12th and 13th-16th. So Chinese qualification predicted strongly at the top of that league and not at all at the bottom — a finer cut, say CFPL top 3 only, might have separated better than treating all five as one block.

entries.notes: listed as invited; also CFPL 3rd as All Gamers

titles.name: Free Fire
titles.description: Two-tier cohort, no Medium: every EWC qualifier from FFWS SEA Spring, FFWS Brazil Split 1 and the FFWS LATAM EWC Qualifier, plus the defending champion, is High. Everyone else is Low.
titles.fieldNote: All 24 trios, with each team's qualifying route traced through the three FFWS regional pages. Several compete under partner-brand names; the canonical column resolves them.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT RULE — THE CLEANEST RESULT IN THE WORKBOOK
seedRationale: THE RULE: High = every EWC qualifier from the three named regional events (FFWS SEA 2026 Spring, FFWS Brazil 2026 Split 1, FFWS LATAM 2026 EWC Qualifier) plus the defending champion EVOS Divine. Low = everyone else. No Medium tier. THE SEPARATION WAS ABSOLUTE. All eight top-eight places went to High seeds. Not one of the ten Low teams finished above 11th. High converted 57% (8 of 14) against a 33% baseline; Low converted 0%. No other title in the workbook has produced a perfect split like this. WHY IT WORKED. The rule is really a regional one — SEA and Brazil dominate Free Fire, and both are represented near the top of the field. The two LATAM qualifiers split the difference: LYON won the whole event, GunDynasty finished 14th. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO is order the top. Six High seeds finished 9th or worse, including the SEA Spring winner Secret WAG in 15th and SEA 4th Aurora in 16th, while SEA 9th Team Falcons finished 6th. So regional qualification predicted membership of the top eight perfectly and position within it not at all — which is exactly the split we keep seeing, in its starkest form yet. Team Secret compete as Secret WAG in FFWS SEA — confirmed, so their SEA Spring 1st place is theirs.
Baseline top-8 rate is 8/24 = 33%. The Medium row stays in place so the tier can be introduced later without restructuring.

entries.notes: competes as Secret WAG in FFWS SEA (confirmed)

titles.name: EA Sports FC 26
titles.description: Run as the FC Pro 26 World Championship. Seeded from EA's official FC Pro World Rankings — pre-event standing reconstructed from the published table, see block 3.
titles.fieldNote: All 36 players. Seed ranks the field by pre-event world ranking; the post-event rank is shown alongside so the movement this tournament caused stays visible.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED SOURCE — EA FC PRO WORLD RANKINGS, AND HOW THE PRE-EVENT TABLE WAS RECOVERED
seedRationale: EA's FC Pro World Rankings are the only official ranking for this title — a publisher-maintained points system covering the whole competitive ecosystem, which is exactly what method A wants. THE TIMING PROBLEM AND THE FIX. The live table is dated 26 July 2026, the final day of this event, and it plainly includes the event's own results: the Change column shows the champion RvPLegend rising 26 places and runner-up levyfinn rising 24. Seeding from it would leak the result into the seed. Because EA publishes that Change column, the pre-event standing can be recovered exactly: pre-event rank = current rank + change. That reverses this tournament's movement and recovers the order as players entered. Seeds here use those reconstructed ranks; both are shown so the movement stays visible. This is derived rather than published, so treat it as method A with a caveat rather than a clean snapshot. WHAT 2026 SHOWED — the worst seed performance of any title in the workbook. Champion RvPLegend entered ranked 30th of the field's pre-event standing. Runner-up levyfinn entered 36th, the LOWEST-ranked player present. Meanwhile world number one Vejrgang finished 5th-8th, number two Emre Yilmaz 17th-24th, and number eight jafonsogv finished 25th. Of the top eight seeds, only two reached the top eight. This is consistent with FC being the title where favourites most reliably fail — the same pattern noted when the portfolio work flagged that FC26's top-8 cohort is unusually affordable precisely because ranking predicts so little.

titles.name: Call of Duty: Black Ops 7
titles.description: Seed method B — the most recent event, the CDL Season 7 Championship. Non-CDL entrants take the bottom seeds because they had no route into that event.
titles.fieldNote: All 16 teams. CDL franchises compete under city-brand names in the league and org names at EWC — both are shown. G2 Esports' 200 points are voided for roster changes past the Deadline.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · SEED — CDL CHAMPIONSHIP, AND THE CLEANEST GROUP SPLIT IN THE WORKBOOK
seedRationale: THE BASIS: the CDL Season 7 Championship, played in Las Vegas in July 2026, three weeks before EWC. It is the most recent competitive meeting of this field and it is exclusive to CDL franchises, which is why the four non-CDL entrants take the bottom seeds — they had no route into it, so there is no form to read. The four CDL franchises that missed those playoffs are seeded 9-12 by regular-season finish. THE GROUP SPLIT WAS PERFECT. All eight CDL Championship playoff teams finished in the EWC top eight. All eight non-playoff and non-CDL teams finished 9th or worse. Not one exception in sixteen. No other title in the workbook has produced a clean binary split like this, and it makes a strong case that CDL participation is the single most informative seed signal available in any title here. THE ORDERING WITHIN THE TOP EIGHT WAS POOR. CDL champions FaZe Vegas, seeded 1st, finished 5th-8th. CDL runners-up OpTic won EWC. Los Angeles Thieves, seeded 8th of the playoff group, took 3rd. So the event told you exactly WHO would contend and almost nothing about the order — the same split seen across the workbook, but with an unusually sharp membership signal. NAMING: CDL franchises use city brands in the league and org names at EWC — FaZe Vegas is FaZe Clan, Riyadh Falcons is Team Falcons, Los Angeles Thieves is 100 Thieves, and so on. Both names are recorded so the mapping is auditable.

titles.name: Rocket League
titles.description: Seeded from RLCS 2026 Rankings, adjusted for regional strength. One seed column (H) feeds the simulator. Regional points are not comparable across regions; the correction is derived entirely from pre-event Majors.
titles.fieldNote: All 16 teams, ordered by the seed used. Adjusted points = regional points × the region multiplier; the multiplier comes from the two 2026 Majors, both played before this event.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · THE REGIONAL ADJUSTMENT — AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE
seedRationale: WHY AN ADJUSTMENT IS NEEDED — decided before looking at any EWC result. RLCS points are earned inside a region, so the number measures performance against regional opposition only. A team can top a weak region on a high total while never having beaten an international field. Comparing those totals directly across regions is not a judgement call about strength; it is a category error in the unit itself. THE CORRECTION IS PRE-EVENT. Liquipedia publishes a regional strength table built from the mean points each region's teams earned at the two 2026 Majors — Boston and Paris — both played BEFORE this event. Normalising to EU = 1.00 gives each region a multiplier: EU 1.00, MENA 0.76, NA 0.55, SAM 0.36, OCE 0.29, APAC 0.23, SSA 0.23. Adjusted points = regional points x multiplier. Every input is prior to EWC, so the seed is a clean statement of pre-event expectation and contains no information about what happened here. WHAT IT CHANGES. Five Fears led SSA on 101 points, more than Team Vitality's 97 in EU; unadjusted they would seed 4th, adjusted 13th. TSM led APAC on 96 and moves from 6th to 15th. Wildcard won OCE on 78 and moves from 12th to 14th. The Notes column records the unadjusted seed wherever it differs by six places or more. POST-HOC OBSERVATION, recorded separately because it played no part in choosing the method: across the 16 teams the adjusted seed tracked the finishing order more closely than the unadjusted one. That is an output of the exercise, not a reason for it. GENERALISES TO OTHER TITLES: the same defect affects Rainbow Six, where SI points treat an APAC slot and a North American slot as equal. Rocket League is the one title where the publisher supplies the cross-region correction ready-made; elsewhere it would have to be constructed.
Regional strength is itself an input — recompute the multipliers from each season's Majors rather than carrying 2026 values forward.

entries.notes: unadjusted points would seed them 15 | canonical join corrected to Ninjas in Pyjamas, matching the Warzone tab

titles.name: Overwatch 2
titles.description: OWCS 2026 Midseason Championship, Paris, 29 July - 2 August. Cohort-seeded by the agreed Stage 2 rule; one cohort column (D) feeds the simulator.
titles.fieldNote: All 16 teams with placement bands, official club points and prize money from the OWCS Midseason Championship prize table. Cohort drives the simulator — edit it directly.
titles.pointsNote: Official EWC Club Championship curve for this title. Points are locked; edit placement only.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT MODEL — STRENGTH WEIGHTS (PLACKETT-LUCE)
seedRationale: THE RULE, agreed before any result was looked at: High = the top 2 of OWCS Korea Stage 2 plus the Stage 2 winners of NA, EMEA and China. Low = the Pacific qualifier and the FACEIT qualifier. Medium = everyone else, including the Japan seed and the EWC title defender. Applied literally to Stage 2 finishing position, so Crazy Raccoon (Korea 2nd) is High even though their EWC slot came from Champions Clash, and T1 (Korea 3rd) is Medium even though they took the second Korea slot.

A cohort is not a rank, it is a STRENGTH WEIGHT. The weight below is a relative odds figure: a High team is treated as three times as likely as a Medium team to be picked next in any given draw, and that ratio does not change if the High cohort grows or shrinks. This is the difference from a band model, where a cohort's implied strength moves when teams are reassigned into it. Cohort size affects how much of the field's total weight a cohort holds, never what an individual team is worth.

The draw itself is Plackett-Luce. Each run, the finishing order is sampled without replacement: the team picked first is chosen with probability proportional to its effective weight, then the next from those remaining, and so on. TVI enters as a temperature: effective weight = w^(1/T), T = TVI/50. A low TVI pushes T below 1, sharpens the weights and makes the favourites win more often; a high TVI flattens them toward a coin-flip field. Change a team's cohort and only that team moves; change the TVI and the whole field's separation moves together.

Sanity check from EWC26: the rule separated poorly at the top. Of the five High teams, two finished top four (ZETA 1st, Weibo 4th) but Virtus.pro went out 9th-12th. Both Low teams finished 13th-16th, which is the part of the rule that did its job.

entries.notes: Korea Stage 2 3rd — took the second Korea slot
Korea Stage 2 2nd; qualified via Champions Clash
EMEA Stage 2 winner — biggest High-cohort miss

titles.name: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS
titles.description: Paris, 21-26 July. 24 teams, group stage into a 16-team Grand Finals under the Smash Rule. Cohort-seeded from the published EWC qualification pathway.
titles.fieldNote: Final standings are the cumulative Grand Finals table after Day 3. The eight teams eliminated in the group stage share 17-24 and score nothing.
titles.pointsNote: Official EWC Club Championship curve for this title. Points are locked; edit placement only.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT MODEL — STRENGTH WEIGHTS (PLACKETT-LUCE)
seedRationale: SEED SOURCE AND WHY IT IS A COHORT. The methodology tab proposed method C (power ranking) for PUBG. There is no cross-comparable public power ranking for this field, so the seed instead comes from the qualification pathway KRAFTON published on 16 June 2026, five weeks before the event. That is a genuine pre-event artefact and it splits the field on exactly the axis that matters: the PGS Points seeds earned their slots on a single global ladder across PGS 1-6, where all 24 teams played the same six events, while the regional seeds earned theirs on regional PGC Points, which are not comparable between regions.

THE RULE. High = the nine PGS Points seeds plus the title defender (Twisted Minds, who competed in the same PGS events and whose PGS slot passed down only because their EWC berth was already secured). Medium = the fourteen regional series seeds, two from each of Americas, China, EMEA, Korea, Rest of APAC, Thailand and Vietnam. Low is unused: nothing in this field qualified through a route weaker than a regional top two. To split the regional seeds further, the regional PGC Points tables give a #1 and #2 per region — worth adding if you want a third band.

The engine is the same Plackett-Luce draw described on the Overwatch 2 tab: weights are relative odds, independent of how many teams sit in a cohort, and the order is sampled without replacement each run. For a battle royale the draw produces a full 1-24 order directly, which suits this title because the points curve runs to 8th rather than in bands.

Sanity check from EWC26: the split was weak. High took 4 of the 8 scoring places from 10 entries (40%) against a 33% baseline, and three PGS-seeded teams did not even reach the Grand Finals. A TVI of 62 is doing most of the work here, which is the honest reading of a battle royale.

entries.notes: topped the group stage on 119 pts, faded in finals

titles.name: MLBB Women's International (MWI)
titles.description: Paris, 14-18 July. Rebranded from Women’s Invitational to Women’s International this year and now the world championship of the women’s circuit. 16 teams, two groups into an eight-team knockout.
titles.fieldNote: All 16 teams. Team Falcons field two entries (Falcons Vega and Falcons Vega MENA); the reconciliation takes the best per club, so only the higher one scores.
titles.pointsNote: Official EWC Club Championship curve for this title. Points are locked; edit placement only.
titles.seedSectionTitle: 3 · COHORT MODEL — STRENGTH WEIGHTS (PLACKETT-LUCE)
seedRationale: SEED CONFIDENCE IS THE LOWEST IN THE WORKBOOK, and the tab should be read that way. The methodology tab proposed method C for this title and flagged thin public data; that flag was right. There is no cross-regional women's ranking and most of the sixteen qualified through single-elimination national or regional qualifiers whose results are not comparable with each other. A cohort is the honest ceiling of what the evidence supports.

PROPOSED RULE — FOR YOUR APPROVAL, not yet agreed. High = organisations with a prior MWI final appearance or a win in the two circuits that have produced every MWI champion, Indonesia and the Philippines: Team Vitality (title defender, 2022, 2023, 2025), Natus Vincere (the roster that won 2024 as Omega Empress) and Falcons Vega (Battle of Gamehers runner-up). Medium = qualifiers from regions that have previously put a team into the MWI knockout stage. Low = first-time and expansion-region qualifiers. Every assignment is visible in column D and is a dropdown, so overrule any of them directly.

The engine is the same Plackett-Luce draw as the other cohort tabs. Because seed confidence is low here and the weights below are deliberately flat, the simulated spread should come out wide — that is the model telling the truth about what we know, not a defect. If you want the spread wider still, raise the TVI rather than compressing the weights: the weights carry the seed, the TVI carries the volatility.

Sanity check from EWC26: two of the three High teams made the final and the third finished 5th-8th, so the top band held. The Low band did not: Falcons Vega MENA reached 5th-8th, which is the assignment most worth revisiting.
Placements 9-16 are recorded as one band. The eight group-stage exits score nothing, and the published sources used do not order them.

workbookReferenceRun.note: 20,000 Monte Carlo runs across all 25 titles. Every run re-draws each title from its seeds alone, scores it on that title’s official points curve, takes each club’s best entry, and sums to a Club Championship table. Nothing from the actual EWC26 results enters the draw; the two right-hand columns are the outcome, shown for comparison only.
